secretReveal.bannerBody: If you close this window without copying it, you will have to generate a new key with {rotate}. Work through the sections: copy the key (step 1), add {file} to the repo (step 2), add the job (step 3).
secretReveal.bannerTitle: The private key is shown only now
secretReveal.diag400: the manifest failed the ICS schema check: binding_id must be a UUID, commit_sha 1 to 64 characters, commit_timestamp a date and bundle_sha256 64 hex characters. The response names the failing field; check the values from --commit-sha / --commit-ts or $CI_COMMIT_SHA.
secretReveal.diag403: the private key in CI does not match the binding. Usually the key was rotated in ICS and the new one never made it into ICS_PRIVATE_KEY. Generate a new one in ICS and replace it.
secretReveal.diag404: the binding was deleted or there is a typo in {id} in {file}. Check that {url} exists.
secretReveal.diag409: commit_timestamp ≤ the last accepted one. Usually after a force push or rebase. Rotate the key in ICS to reset the binding's monotonic clock.
secretReveal.diagKeyMissing: the CLI got a path, but there is no file there. Usually {name} is not passed to this job at all: a protected variable on an unprotected branch, or an environment scope that does not match the job.
secretReveal.diagNoFile: {name} is a plain Variable (text), so after the {at} the CLI got the key itself instead of a path. Change the type of {name} in GitLab to {file} or remove the {at} before {variable} in the command.
secretReveal.diagPull: your runner tries to authenticate to the registry. The image {image} is publicly readable: check for a custom {config} with a wrong password or forced authentication on the runner. As a last resort, pull with a personal access token.
secretReveal.fieldBindingId: UUID assigned by ICS when the binding was created (above). It identifies the binding on the server; do not change it.
secretReveal.fieldEndpoint: the ICS URL. For your instance: {endpoint}. You can also leave it empty: the CLI reads {variable}, so you can define a CI/CD Variable (Text) instead of hard-coding it in the file.
secretReveal.fieldEntrypoint: disables the image's default entrypoint (the ics-sync binary itself) so GitLab Runner can run its own script.
secretReveal.fieldExclude: optional list of globs left out of the bundle. Typical: node_modules/**, dist/**, *.test.*. Git metadata (.git) is always left out.
secretReveal.fieldImage: {image}: publicly readable in the Container Registry, so the runner pulls it without credentials.
secretReveal.fieldKind: for people reading the file only: the CLI does not send it. ICS checks the uploaded content against the document's own type ({collection}, {single}, {bundle}). For this document: {kind}.
secretReveal.fieldPrivateKey: the {at} prefix tells the CLI that the variable holds the path of a PEM file (File-type variable). If {name} is a plain Variable (Text), use {plain} without {at}.
secretReveal.fieldPublicKey: the public key of this key pair. ICS verifies against the key in its database anyway, but having the field lets anyone check that they match.
secretReveal.fieldPullPolicy: forces a fresh image pull. Without it some runners keep a stale cached :1 and run the old binary after a release. If your runner has allowed_pull_policies=["if-not-present"], remove this field and pin a SHA tag instead of :1.
secretReveal.fieldRules: the sync runs only for pushes to the default branch (usually main). You can extend it, e.g. with tags or MR pipelines.
secretReveal.fieldSource: path of the published content relative to the job's working directory (in GitLab CI the repo root), not to this file. "." = the whole repo, "docs/" = one folder, "dist/" = a build artifact from another job.
secretReveal.fieldTags: the runner must support Docker (docker executor or dind). Adjust to your instance's tags.
secretReveal.fieldTitle: for people reading the file only: the CLI does not send it and the document keeps its title in ICS.
secretReveal.fileTypeNote: In CI a File-type variable is exposed as the {path} to a temporary file, not as the value. That is why the CLI in step 3 gets {arg}: the {at} prefix tells it "this is the path of a PEM file, read it".
secretReveal.jobNote: {lead} it packs {source} into a deterministic tar.gz, computes the SHA-256, signs the manifest with the Ed25519 key and sends a multipart POST to {url}. ICS verifies the signature, checks the hash and replay (the commit timestamp must grow monotonically) and creates a new version of the document.
secretReveal.jobNoteLead: What this job does after a push:
secretReveal.step1Title: Copy the private key to GitLab CI/CD variables
secretReveal.step1Where: In the repo project on GitLab: {path}.
secretReveal.step2Intro: You commit this file in the open: it holds the {id} and the {public} key (PEM), never the private one.
secretReveal.varFlagsHint: limits access to protected branches and tags (usually main); the branch must be marked as protected in Settings → Repository
secretReveal.varKeyHint: exactly this name, the snippet in step 3 uses it
secretReveal.varScopeHint: matches every job by default; if you use environments, narrow it to the one that runs the sync
secretReveal.varTypeHint: MUST be File. The CLI also accepts a plain Variable (text); then use $ICS_PRIVATE_KEY instead of @$ICS_PRIVATE_KEY in step 3
secretReveal.varValueHint: the whole block, from BEGIN to END inclusive
secretReveal.varVisibilityHint: GitLab cannot mask File-type variables (a PEM has disallowed characters and line breaks), but a File-type variable never prints its value in logs, so it is safe anyway
securityFindings.criticalBody: The bundle contains patterns such as eval(), javascript: or external scripts. It renders on an isolated subdomain, but review the content before publishing.
securityFindings.warnBody: The bundle contains higher-risk patterns (inline event handlers, document.write). It renders on an isolated subdomain, which is usually safe, but consider refactoring.

userDetail.deleteConfirmMessage.other: The account is deleted together with {count} documents and all links. This cannot be undone.

userDetail.deleteDesc.one: Deletes the account with {count} document and all share links. This cannot be undone. The audit log keeps an entry (with the number of deleted documents).
userDetail.deleteDesc.other: Deletes the account with {count} documents and all share links. This cannot be undone. The audit log keeps an entry (with the number of deleted documents).

userDetail.lockDesc: A temporary sign-in lock. The account comes back on its own when it expires. The reason goes to the audit log.
userDetail.quotaDesc: Total size of the current versions of all documents. Older versions do not count.
userDetail.reinviteDesc: A new e-mail with a fresh invite token. The old token stays valid until its seven days run out; whichever is used first wins.
userDetail.resetDesc: Send the user an e-mail with a link to set a new password. Works only for email and password accounts.
userDetail.revokeTokensDesc: Revokes all personal access tokens of this person. Agents and scripts lose access right away.
userDetail.roleDescAdmin: Full access: users, HTML bundle approval, document types and the audit log.
userDetail.roleDescExternal: Someone outside the organisation; addresses outside the allowed domains get this role automatically. The permissions are the same as a user's: what was shared with them and their projects. Google sign-in depends on the e-mail domain, not on the role.
userDetail.roleDescUser: Staff member: documents, projects and sharing.
